name.text: Graphing a bounded segment with mixed inequality signs

questiontext.text:
Solve the following compound inequality for \(x\):

\( \displaystyle {@L@} < {@a@}x - {@b@} \le {@U@} \)

a) The algebraic Solution:

(Enter the numerical bounds in the boxes below.)

[[input:ans1]] \( < x \le \) [[input:ans2]]

Lower Limit: [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]
Upper Limit: [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

b) Represent this solution interval on the number line below. Drag the two points to the correct boundary values.

(Note: The left boundary is a strict inequality (\(<\)), so the open (unshaded) circle is used. The right boundary is an inclusive inequality (\(\le\)), so the closed (shaded) circle is used.)

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

Part a: The algebraic Solution

To solve the continuous compound inequality, we isolate \(x\) by applying operations to all three parts simultaneously.

First, we group the constant terms by adding \({@b@}\) to all three parts:

\( \displaystyle \begin{aligned} {@L@} + {@b@} &< {@a@}x \le {@U@} + {@b@} \\ {@L + b@} &< {@a@}x \le {@U + b@} \end{aligned} \)

Next, we divide all three parts by the coefficient of \(x\), which is \({@a@}\):

\( \displaystyle \begin{aligned} \frac{{@L + b@}}{{@a@}} &< x \le \frac{{@U + b@}}{{@a@}} \\ {@ta1@} &< x \le {@ta2@} \end{aligned} \)

Hence, the correct algebraic solution is:

\( \displaystyle \boxed{{@ta1@} < x \le {@ta2@}} \)

Part b: Graphical Representation

To represent this on a number line, we must match the circles to the specific inequality signs:

  • For the lower limit \({@ta1@}\), the inequality is strict (\(<\)), so we use an open (unshaded) circle.
  • For the upper limit \({@ta2@}\), the inequality is inclusive (\(\le\)), so we use a closed (shaded) circle.

We then draw a solid line segment connecting the two circles.
